name: When the Self Turns Against the Self - An experential workshop on healing and understanding the painwhich arises in the self
description:
This workshop re-examines the concept of the "self" from an experiential perspective rather than a purely cognitive one, addressing how individuals experience and understand emotional pain. It opens with fundamental inquiry into how one recognizes when they are not okay and what true emotional well-being actually means. The session highlights a pervasive issue: modern approaches often focus excessively on pain in inaccurate ways, leading to a lost connection with the core concept of self. Instead of treating emotional distress as an abstract idea, the module aims to ground self-awareness in real, felt internal experiences.  Ultimately, the workshop serves as a gateway to help individuals navigate deep-seated pain, break free from restrictive emotional patterns, and reconstruct a grounded, present sense of self.   
The workshop is being organized and moderated by Nimesh George ANd Gokul R who are practicing psychologist based in Bangalore

name: Coffee and Conversations - Meetup
description:
What about some Filter Coffee and Unfiltered conversations on a fine Sunday morning?

Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment.

We at Listeners Circle are committed to building a community where there are no unsaid words, held-back emotions and buried feelings because of the fear of being judged.

After 50+ Editions of Tell Your Story, Listeners Circle is relaunching a lighter format - Coffee and Conversations!
Coffee lightens us up. Coffee gives us clarity. Coffee refreshes. Sip a coffee and speak your heart out without fear of judgment, and listen without judging! Coffee is on us, and the onus of conversation without judgment is on you.

Every word matters. Every emotion matters. Every feeling matters.
Think about how it would feel to take an hour out of your fast-paced life and share your experiences and thoughts to people who listen to you without judging over a cup of Coffee? Also, listen to others without judging.
Listeners' Circle Coffee and Conversations -This is an event to make that happen.

Be a part of the Listener's Circle Coffee & Conversations - Edition 5.
Speak your mind without being judged. Speak your mind without any boundaries. No photography and videography without consent. Your stories stay within the four walls of the room and the hearts.
Would you like to just listen? We have a place for you too.
Book your passes in advance to avoid the last-minute sell outs.
Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment. We have done 50+ sessions over the last year, enabling people to voice their stories. Coffee & Conversations is our new format based on popular demand.

name: Queer Quiet Hours - Meetup
description:
Queer Quiet Hours returns for September 2026!
Register here: http://bit.ly/adhdqueeple
A soft little corner for LGBTQIA+ folks to slow down, make art, read, journal, daydream, or simply exist in shared company.
There’s no pressure to interact. Come with your own project, or just arrive as you are. We’ll also have art materials around for anyone who wants to use them.
✨ This space is for LGBTQIA+ folks only. We haven’t opened it up to allies yet. Thank you for understanding.

⏰ Sundays, 2 - 5 PM
📍 @attagalatta, Indiranagar, Bangalore
📸 No photos taken without clear consent.

name: A Special Day - Film Screening
description: On the day of Hitler's historical 1938 visit to Rome, a resigned housewife and a homosexual journalist form a strong bond over their shared suffering under Mussolini's fascist regime.

name: Science Café - Meetup
description:
Welcome to the September Edition of the AG Science Café. 
The theme for our conversations will be "Photography - Science and Art of Perception". 
We will explore the role of photography, its history and how it has shaped our perception about the world we live in, how imaging and image processing has enhanced scientific vision and documented history. 
Do bring in your favourite photographs,  powerful images and stories of and about photography. This will be a deferred celebration of World Photography Day.

name: An Invitation to Slow Down ✨ - Silent Reading Hour
description:
When everything feels busy and overwhelming, this is your invitation to pause, unplug, and rest.
Bring the book you have been meaning to read and spend a quiet evening reading in the comfort and warmth of community support. Reading together in silence helps us stay present, cultivate a regular reading habit, and feel deeply connected—without any of the pressure of constant conversation.
After our reading hour, we will open up a gentle space to share book recommendations, exchange thoughts, and discover what others are reading over shared stories.
To keep this experience intimate, meaningful, and welcoming, spots are limited.

name: TransLate - A talk about the lived experiences of transgender individuals
description:
TransLate: Talks by Trans People, is a storytelling platform where transgender individuals share lived experiences — not limited to “exceptional” success stories but inclusive of the everyday realities of survival, joy, and resistance. 
Since its inception in 2023, TransLate has already become a space of both celebration and change. Our first two editions in Hyderabad brought together 80+ and 60+ participants respectively, featuring respected voices such as Dr. Kiran B Nayak and Vyjayanti Mogli. This is our first edition in Bangalore.
Through this intentional gathering of experiences, identities find affirmation and the painful grip of isolation begins to loosen, replaced by the profound recognition of shared humanity. Each narrative becomes an act of quiet revolution, dismantling the walls of stereotype and shame that have long confined trans existence to margins and whispers. TransLate honors the profound courage embedded in daily survival, the simple, radical act of moving through the world as one's authentic self. In this collective witnessing, something transformative occurs: individual wounds begin to heal within the larger body of community, and what was once endured in solitude becomes a source of shared strength, pride, and unwavering solidarity. 
About For&Bi: For&Bi is a transgender-led collective based in Hyderabad and Bangalore. Our mission is to create safe, inclusive spaces that elevate marginalized voices and build bridges of solidarity across communities. Our work centers not only on advocacy and visibility but also on collective care, resilience, and trans joy as antidotes to stigma, violence, and exclusion.

name: Homo and Juliet - Book Signing
description:
Join us for an exclusive book signing session as part of the national #HomoJulietBookTour!
Dr. Shruti Chakravarty, an author, therapist, and queer-feminist activist, brings her groundbreaking collection of queer lesbian love stories, Homo and Juliet, directly to readers. Come hear about the stories, meet the author, and get your copies personally signed.
About the book: 
Homo and Juliet, offers an archive of queer living through eight real-life love stories featuring lesbian couples and non-binary individuals. Moving beyond rigid heteronormative templates, the book explores the quiet, radical work of building chosen families, navigating natal family dynamics, and finding authentic joy, care, and resistance in everyday intimacy.

name: BHAJAN CLUBBING FOR KIDS🎶✨👶👧 - A fun-filled evening where music meets mythology
description:
A fun-filled evening where music meets mythology! Join us for an interactive session of soulful bhajans, engaging stories, and lots of laughter!
About the hosts:
Priya Mani is the creator of The Little Shloka Book Series (now in over 50,000 homes worldwide), a breathwork coach with The Art of Living Foundation, and founder of Little Desi—a creative space dedicated to making ancient Indian wisdom fun, beautiful, and relatable.
She tells stories that may remind you of your grandma, and her superpower is making world-class rasam!
Anagha Karvir is a full-time musician, breathwork and meditation coach, trained Kathak dancer, and founder of Ana & Co.
After 16 years in the corporate world creating learning and leadership experiences, she now creates meaningful experiences through music, movement, stories, and breath.
Her superpower is helping people feel comfortable enough to participate, connect and let their guard down—whether at a concert, workshop, dance floor or bhajan gathering.

name: Big Feelings, Little Hearts - A Parent-Child Workshop
description:
Big feelings can be hard for little ones to understand—and even harder to express.
In this interactive parent-child workshop by My Big Feelings, children and parents will explore emotions through conversations and playful activities. Together, they’ll learn to name emotions, notice how feelings show up in the body, and discover simple ways to express and manage big feelings safely.
The workshop is designed to create a fun, judgment-free space where children can talk about what they feel, while parents learn simple tools they can continue using at home.

name: BUILD - A Theatre Performance for Young Audiences with Sticks and Clay
description:
BUILD is a non-verbal theatre performance for young auidences inspired by the open-ended games children create when left to their own devices. Two young people, one with sticks and the other with clay, explore the possibilities of play while creating and connecting. They encounter the different sizes, textures and shapes of their materials, offer them sounds, find a rhythm and discover ways of being together while embarking on a journey of music and movements.
Age Group - 2 to 5

name: A Little Something - Book launch
description:
Join us for an evening of simple, soul- gripping poetry, amidst light banter and laughter. Whether you're here to recite or to just listen, let the poetry resonate with you as we reminisce over those little things that occupy huge spaces in our lives.
You are invited to the launch of 'A little something' - a book of poems by Sreeja Mohandas, at Atta Galatta, Indiranagar, Bangalore, on the 19th of September, from 6 to 8 p.m

name: Build an archive of family rituals - Art Workshop
description:
Some family stories are told again and again. Others live in shared meals, festive traditions, bedtime routines, and inside jokes—rituals that shape how we remember one another.
Through a series of creative prompts, you'll reflect on the stories and rituals that tell your family's story, then interpret them in your own way through words, illustrations, mixed media, or a medium of your choice.
You can add your work to a living archive of family rituals, built through gatherings in different places, and take your creation home.
About the host:
Presented by Mysticeti, a creative studio that brings people together through stories, creative experiences, and community, this workshop is inspired by Bapa Wants Fish, Mysticeti's new children's book about the comfort and grounding that family rituals can offer during times of uncertainty. Facilitated by Stuti Sareen, founder, Mysticeti.

name: Ghichi Pichi - A playful, facilitated introduction to mixed media art.
description:
Before you rush to make “art”, come meet the materials. Let’s do some fun Ghichi Pichi with colours, textures and explore mark-making with me, Jade.
Let’s throw away the rule books and spend some time in free play, with plenty of materials and other folks exploring alongside us.
In these sessions, I will guide you through mixed-media art and mark-making.Mixed media art is all about mixing different types of colours (wet or dry) to create artworks.  And Mark-making is making marks—lines, shapes, patterns and more—on a surface.
Mark-making can be a soothing sensory way to slow down and simply enjoy yourself.
No pressure to make “good art” or be productive. No urgency. No prior skills needed.

name: Dear Diary, WTF - Journaling Session for Women
description:
Women are shamed for doing it all and shamed for taking a break, so there's no winning when we leave it to society. Enough with the guilt.
​Wherever you are in your career, the constant pressure to prove yourself can be exhausting, even when the work fulfils you. So this session isn't about "calming down" or "relaxing." It's about raging tf out with art and journaling, getting all that noise out of your head and onto paper.
​What to expect


​A guided art journaling session — part writing, part making, all unfiltered


​No art or journaling experience needed


​A women-only room, so you can be as honest as you like


​All supplies provided (journal, art materials, the works)


​Your facilitator Yukti Grover is an Expressive Arts Facilitator and the founder of Your Journal Project. Through journaling, writing, and simple art practices, she helps people create without pressure and has run workshops across Bengaluru, including at Atta Galatta and the Bengaluru Poetry Festival.
​Details Date: Sunday, September 20, 2026 Time: 1 p.m. Venue: Atta Galatta, Bengaluru Price: ₹799 (includes all supplies)
​Hosted by Women in Product Marketing (WIPM) x Your Journal Project.
​Seats are limited. Just bring yourself.

name: The Gathering Room - Support Group
description:
Divorce and separation don't end when the papers do. There's the decision itself. The legal process. And then everything after it: the parenting schedule you're renegotiating, the finances you're untangling, the boundaries you're still learning how to hold.
Somewhere in all of it, a story tends to settle in: that this is a failure, that it has to get ugly, that there's a "right" way to grieve or move on.
This session starts from a different premise. A relationship changing shape isn't a verdict on you, and it doesn't have to look like a battle to be real.
This afternoon is for all of you, mid-decision, past it, or still arriving.
The Format
This isn't a talk or a lecture.
Expect movement, a few structured group activities done in pairs or as a full group, and space throughout to simply notice where you are. No performance, no scripts, nothing to prepare.
What to Expect
Arrival
Come whenever you're ready. No forms to fill, no small talk required, and nothing you owe anyone an explanation for.
Opening Circle
Seema, who's facilitating the session, will say a quick hello and walk you through how the afternoon unfolds, including what happens inside the activities. If you feel like sharing a word about why you're here, you can. If you'd rather just listen, that's completely fine too.
The Heart of the Session
This is the main part of the afternoon: some movement, a few activities done in pairs or as a group, and quieter moments in between just to notice how you're feeling. Nobody's asking you to talk if you don't want to. Nobody's asking you to perform, either.
Coming Back Together
Before we close, we'll gather again as a full group, just to sit with whatever came up. Sharing a reflection or a small gesture is welcome.
Closing
You might leave with a bit more clarity. You might leave without having said a single word, and still feel a little less alone. Either way is exactly right.
This is the first of what we hope becomes a monthly gathering.
What's not included
Anything from Atta Galatta's bookstore or café- that one's on you (though we'd happily recommend a coffee on your way out)

name: Unwind with Origami - Explore the Japanese art of paper folding
description:
About the Workshop:
 Learn to transform simple sheets of paper into something magical — take home your beautiful creations.
· A hands-on workshop led by the artist-duo Nikhil and Krithika
· Checkout their Instagram Page “niksorigami” to see their work! Link: https://www.instagram.com/niksorigami/
Who is it for? Ages 8 - 80+. Origami is for all - Kids & Adults welcome! A mindful activity for adults to relax. A fun activity for kids to learn a new skill!
Why join?
· Unwind & relax — A mindful break from your everyday routine
· Spend quality time together— A great way to bond with your partner, family, or friends. Or meet new people at the workshop!
· Try something new— Discover a creative hobby you can take home with you
· Explore the benefits of origami – improves creativity, focus, hand-eye coordination, patience, memory. The list goes on!
What’s included? Each participant gets an envelope of high-quality, assorted origami papers to fold with. Origami needs nothing else – Just paper, your hands, patience, and some magic!
About the Artists:
Nikhil & Krithika are a husband-and-wife artist duo who love creating and teaching origami together. With 120+ origami workshops conducted, they bring plenty of experience — and lots of enthusiasm — to every session. Nikhil has also authored a book in origami – “Stellar Origami Nakshatras – Volume 1” available globally on Amazon.

name: Heartbeat Unscripted X BB Ki Crimes 🎭 - Theatre Performance
description:
HEARTBeat Improv proudly presents two Comedy Shows, THE DOUBLE TROUBLE - An electrifying, two act unscripted evening bringing together spontaneous theatre, sharp satire, and edge of your seat comedy all under one ticket.

📊 ACT 1: HEARTBeat Unscripted 7 - ON SCREEN, OFF SCRIPT

Ever had to present a slide deck you’ve never seen before in your life? Our improvisers take the stage to tackle completely unseen, surprise slide presentations projected live on screen. Watch them navigate absurd charts, random topics, and bizarre visuals with pure wit and unflinching corporate confidence.

🕵️ ACT 2: BB ki Crimes - Unscripted Mystery Thriller
An improvised whodunit murder mystery comedy featuring Ashok, Rashmi, and Kushagr! Driven entirely by audience suggestions, this trio crafts a gripping tale packed with wild characters, shocking motives, hilarious twists, and a dramatic live reveal.

WHY YOU SHOULD BE THERE:
• 100% Unscripted & Spontaneous: Everything is made up live on the spot.
•Your Are Important: Your prompts & suggestions shape the stories and the scenes.
• Free Snacks on Us: Enjoy complimentary crunchy munchies provided by our snacking partner, BRB Popped Chips.
• Warm Community Vibe: A welcoming, high energy live theatre experience right in the heart of Indiranagar.

Come for the slide chaos, stay for the murder mystery, and enjoy a full evening of unscripted entertainment!

name: Book Conversations - Book Discussion
description:
Join us for an intimate evening of ideas and stories as Archana Jain (The Human Premium, Fungibility) and Llaher Jain (Sketches of a Heavy Mind) come together for a thought‑provoking book conversation.
Together, they will share their journeys as writers, exchange perspectives across generations, and invite the audience into a dialogue on how literature can illuminate human potential and the art of creating value in a changing world.

name: Zadanchya Manat Jau - Marathi Poetry Evening
description:
Tickets available on Phone Booking Only. For tickets contact - (Girish) - 9890606250 / (Apurva) - 9730345746. 
Embark on a poetic journey into the minds of trees where verse and music intertwine to explore nature’s resilience and humanity’s impact. 
What if trees could share their thoughts? What would they feel when a bird perches on their branches, when rain caresses their leaves, or when they sense the threat of an axe?  ‘Zadanchya Manat Jaau’ – ‘Into the Minds of Trees’ – invites you to experience these reflections and more, offering a heartfelt tribute to every tree on the planet. 
This performance celebrates trees as the first poetry of Mother Earth, honoring their quiet strength and the profound connection between nature and humanity. Performed by Abolee Deshpande, Girish Datar & Apurva Kulkarni, ‘Zadanchya Manaat Jaau’ brings the voices of trees to life through poetry and music. Drawing from the works of renowned poets, the production blends Marathi and Hindi prose and songs in perfect harmony, creating an emotional narrative that resonates with every listener. 
Through vivid imagery and lyrical reflections, this moving production paints a poignant portrait of the delicate bond between humans and the natural world. Simple yet thought provoking, it invites you to pause and reflect on the beauty, resilience and vulnerability of trees. It’s a celebration of nature’s silent poetry and powerful reminder of our shared responsibility to nurture and protect Earth for generations to come.   
‘Zadanchya Manat Jaau’ is a tribute to every tree living on this planet—a homage to the first poetry of Mother Earth: the tree. 
The Team:
Abolee Deshpande – Performer  
Girish Datar - Performer
Apurva Kulkarni - Performer 
Neha Joshee - Music Operation
Compilation                    -        Apurva Kulkarni, Girish Datar

name: Food In Literature - Book Club
description:
Food is more than something we eat; it is a record of culture, memory, and the places we come from. In Forgotten Foods, we journey through overlooked ingredients, lost recipes, and disappearing culinary traditions, uncovering the stories and communities behind them. What can rediscovering these forgotten foods teach us about history, identity, and the changing ways we nourish ourselves?
Book of the month: Forgotten Foods.
Edited by Siobhan Lambert-Hurley, Tarana Husain Khan and Claire Chambers
When: Saturday, 26th September, 2026 at 11 a.m.
Where: Atta Galatta Bookstore, Indira Nagar
Ages: 18+
Hosted by: Prachi Grover
Registration is mandatory as we have limited spots.
The session is free & copies of the book are available at the store. 
Prachi Grover is a culinary consultant and educator and is the founder of “From Words to Wok,” a community for people who love to read and eat.

name: AG Lit Sisters Presents: Our City, That Year - Thematic Book Club
description:
For this month's theme, we're exploring the relationship between literature, identity, and the places we call home.
The reading prompt is simple but fun: members are invited to pick a book with the name of their state in the title. It can be the state they were born in, grew up in, belong to, or have eventually made their home. We'll then come together to discuss the books, our personal associations with these places, and the different ways literature represents them.
As always, readers are welcome and non-readers are celebrated. The meeting is open to anyone who enjoys stories and conversations, whether or not they've completed a book.

name: Watercolor Florals - Art Workshop
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta on 26 September for a hands-on watercolour workshop exploring the beauty of loose, flowy floral painting.
We'll begin with a series of painting warmups to get comfortable with the brush, water and pigments. You will then learn techniques for creating beautiful flowers through flowing washes, colour blending and simple shapes, before putting these techniques together to paint your own floral composition.
You can take home all your finished paintings/artworks.
No prior experience is required. All painting materials will be provided, so just come ready to experiment, paint and have fun!

name: BWW Short Story Community - short story community
description:
The BWW Short Fiction Community at Atta Galatta will discuss
The Narayans
By Akhil Sharma
The Narayans by Akhil Sharma is an emotionally precise look at memory, distance, and human connection in an age of digital noise. Set against a sudden break from technology, Sharma’s evocative prose captures how individuals navigate their private inner worlds and attempt to find meaning in simple, low-tech moments.
Read the text and come to the event.

name: Children of Heaven - Film Screening
description: Ali has lost his sister Zohre's shoes. They are poor, and need to get the shoes before someone finds out. Ali gets the grand idea of participating in a race to win new shoes for Zohre.

name: Read A Kitaab - Book Club
description:

name: A Storywalk through Indiranagar - Storytelling
description:
On a Saturday morning, walk through the lanes of Indiranagar with Vikram Sridhar to discover the area through its folklore, heritage, and ecology. The walk will begin and end at Atta Galatta. The tales will revolve around historical, mythical, and personal narratives woven as we discover the area through the walk.

name: Earth Tales  - Book Launch
description: Celebrating India’s relationship with nature and the communities that help sustain it, the afternoon will feature a folk music performance, dramatised readings of folktales from across the country, conversations on ecology, and the launch of Earth Tales by the Centre for Contemporary Folklore, published by Duckbill, an imprint of Penguin Random House India. We welcome folklore enthusiasts of all ages!

name: We Matched, Unfortunately  - Book Lauch
description:
Join us for the launch of We Matched, Unfortunately, a humorous and heartfelt anthology featuring real stories about modern dating, awkward matches, unexpected connections, and everything that happens when romance doesn’t quite go according to plan!
The evening will feature storytelling by the book’s contributors and guests, along with interactive dating-themed games such as Dating Taboo, Do You Know Your Gen Z Dating Terms?, and Dating Bingo. Expect funny stories, lively conversations, prizes, and plenty of relatable dating moments.

name: Where Creativity meets Everyday style - Tote Bag Painting Workshop
description:
Join Bangalore-based artist Angana Phookan for an immersive Tote Bag Painting Workshop on 10 October. Explore colours, patterns, and artistic expression as you design a tote that reflects your personal style. Whether you're an art enthusiast or simply looking to try something new, this workshop is for you.
Create something beautiful. Make it uniquely yours.

name: Authentic Relating Games  - Playful yet deep games to help people connect
description:
Ever wonder what is possible when we drop the small talk and connect for real?

Authentic Relating Games is a global practice of guided, playful yet deep exercises (the 'games') designed to help people connect more honestly and meaningfully — whether with close friends or complete strangers.

Through structured partner and group conversations, you will get to practice speaking from the heart, deep listening, and noticing what's alive in you as you relate to others.  The games create space for more honesty, curiosity, and real human connection — often in ways that feel surprisingly fun, refreshing, and profoundly moving.

What to Expect

- A Structured Container:  We will start as a full group to set some simple guidelines that ensure the space feels safe, respectful, and confidential.
- Activities with Partners, Trios, and the Large Group: We'll keep changing partners throughout the session (no need to bring a partner!).
- Guided Prompts and Demos: We'll guide you step-by-step through the games and provide live demonstrations so you know what to do.
- Total Autonomy: You are always in the driver's seat.  You choose how deeply you want to go, or pass on a prompt or game at any time.
- A New Set of Games: If you attended Authentic Relating Games previously, don't worry this won't be the same games but a different set of activities to explore!

No experience needed.  Come as you are.  If you've never done anything like this before, don't worry — it's simple and there is no pressure to get it "right".

About the facilitator:
Roy Jacob is the founder of the Conscious Communication Academy and has been facilitating workshops and retreats for over 15 years, mostly for changemakers as well as team retreats for NGOs and companies.  Roy grew up in the U.S. before finding his calling and coming to India (where his roots are) in 2003.  He believes in the transformative power of combining radical honesty with radical care.
